svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A few individuals arrive in a new habitat with limited resources."], [1, "Lag phase: numbers grow slowly while the individuals settle and reach breeding age."], [3.5, "Exponential phase: resources are plentiful, so the birth rate far exceeds the death rate."], [7, "Transitional phase: limiting factors such as food, space and predators slow the growth."], [10, "Plateau: the birth rate equals the death rate, and the population stays near the carrying capacity K."]]
svg.title: Population growth: the S-curve
svg.desc: A logistic population growth curve with lag, exponential, transitional and plateau phases, approaching the carrying capacity K.
svg.text: Logistic model. Real populations fluctuate around K.

g.data-info: Few individuals; they are adapting and maturing, so numbers rise slowly.
Plenty of food and space: the birth rate is much higher than the death rate, so numbers double at a steady rate.
Limiting factors (food, space, competition, predation, disease, waste) start to act: the growth rate slows.
Birth rate = death rate. The population fluctuates around the carrying capacity.
Number of individuals against time for a population in a new, limited environment.
The largest population the environment can support for a long time.
